paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The Sabbath was never meant to be a weight on your back. Jesus says, "The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath." (Mark 2:27) God gave it as a gift, and the Pharisees were treating it like a clipboard.

Then Jesus says, "Therefore, the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath." (Mark 2:28) Think about that. The One who is Lord of the day is standing right there in the synagogue, asking, "Which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?" (Mark 3:4) And the people watching Him couldn't even answer, because they were so busy watching for a reason to accuse Him.

That's the part that gets me. A hardness of heart can sit in a room full of religious people and still miss the man who needs help. Jesus looked at them with anger and sorrow, and then He restored that hand anyway. So ask yourself, baker: am I holding the rules, or am I holding the Lord of the rules? Keep your eyes on Him, and the good will follow.
